item.title: AI Job Losses: A Guide to the Proposals for Helping Workers
item.description: Guaranteed income. AI dividends. ‘Basic compute.’ Here are the proposed solutions if the technology wipes out millions of jobs.

item.title: Shell Trader Mansfield Resigns After 26 Years at Oil Major
item.description: Shell Plc veteran Geoffrey Mansfield has resigned from his role as global desk lead for low-carbon fuels trading, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: Milei ante gran desafío electoral: el desempleo crece en Argentina
item.description: La economía argentina crece y la inflación cede, pero el empleo formal sigue cayendo. La pérdida de puestos de trabajo y el aumento de la informalidad se perfilan como una de las mayores amenazas para la reelección de Javier Milei.

item.title: Argentina Job Losses, Unemployment Are Milei’s Big Political Risk
item.description: President Javier Milei lowered inflation and poverty in Argentina, while eliminating its budget deficit. But the nation’s labor market is still mired in the crisis he was elected to confront.

item.title: Libyan Protests Flare as Government Struggles to Keep Lights On
item.description: Protests broke out again in the Libyan capital after the energy-rich country suffered its third widespread blackout in two days, fueling public anger over deteriorating basic services.

item.title: Iceland Hikes Key Rate to 8% to Lower Risk of Prices Spiraling
item.description: Iceland’s central bank raised borrowing costs for the third time this year as rising fuel costs due to the Iran war risk further feeding a wage-price spiral.

item.title: Egypt Bond Risk at 2014 Low Shows Decade of Debt Distress Easing
item.description: Record foreign-currency reserves and a vote of confidence from the International Monetary Fund have cut Egypt’s risk premium to the lowest since 2014.

item.title: South Africa Inflation Cools, Making Case to Hold Rates
item.description: South African annual inflation eased more than expected in July, hardening the argument for the central bank to keep interest rates on hold as it assesses the fallout from the Iran war.

item.title: Pakistan’s Record IPO Year Gets Boost From SE Fruits Listing
item.description: Fresh produce company SE Fruits and Vegetable Ltd. is planning an initial public offering in Pakistan next month to boost its export capacity, adding to a record year of listings in the country.

item.title: Bank Indonesia’s New Chief Signals Continuity, Focus on Rupiah
item.description: Indonesia’s central bank held its policy rate steady in the first monetary decision under acting Governor Destry Damayanti, who stuck close to past guidance and vowed to uphold the stability of the rupiah.

item.title: Lagarde Says Europe Can’t Afford to Miss Out on AI Revolution
item.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde warned that the region mustn’t get left behind as artificial intelligence transforms the global economy.

item.title: SK Hynix Moves to Calm Market With $29 Billion Share Buyback
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. unveiled plans to buy back 40 trillion won ($29 billion) of stock and return more of its profits to shareholders in an effort to calm worries about the durability of AI spending.

item.title: Adnoc Cuts to Murban Volumes Send Flagship Oil Grade Higher
item.description: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. plans to trim the amount of crude sold to Asian customers in August and September, according to people familiar with the matter — cuts that are already helping to push up the price of the flagship Murban oil grade.

item.title: Australia Rejects Far-Right Call to Slash Cigarette Taxes by 75%
item.description: Australia’s government rejected the far right One Nation party’s call to slash cigarette taxes in order to reduce prices and cut crime, arguing instead for an intensified struggle against illegal tobacco flooding the country.

item.title: Optimism on Europe Returns to Pre-Iran War Highs: Taking Stock
item.description: Investors increasingly favor European stocks over US peers as the region’s robust economic outlook proves more attractive at a time of surging AI spending.

item.title: India Stocks Top Indonesia as Asia’s Least-Favored in BofA Poll
item.description: India has replaced Indonesia as Asia’s least-preferred stock market in a survey of fund managers by Bank of America Corp., signaling growing caution toward a market that’s among the world’s worst performers this year.

item.title: UK Inflation Climbs to Four-Month High as Energy Bills Rise
item.description: UK inflation accelerated in July after energy bills surged, ending a short period of respite for hard-pressed British households.

item.title: South Korea Exploring New Financial Hub Beyond Overcrowded Seoul
item.description: South Korea is looking to create a new financial center outside the capital Seoul, as the government moves to ease over-concentration in the greater metropolitan area, which is home to more than half the country’s population.

item.title: Ethiopia’s Currency Sinks as Central Bank Burns Through Dollars
item.description: Ethiopia is burning through billions of dollars in a frantic — and so far unsuccessful — bid to stem the selloff in its currency.

item.title: Korea Yield Curve Steepest Since 2021 as Long-Bond Slump Deepens
item.description: The spread between South Korea’s three- and 10-year government bond yields has widened to the highest in nearly five years amid a global selloff in long-dated securities and expectations that Bank of Korea won’t raise interest rates aggressively.

item.title: Worker Influx Lifts Hong Kong Population as Birth Slump Worsens
item.description: Hong Kong is increasingly reliant on imported workers as births fell below 30,000 for the first time, underscoring the limits of government incentives to arrest a demographic slump that threatens the city’s future workforce.

item.title: FTSE 100 Live: Futures Ease as Global Stocks Fall
item.description: FTSE 100 Live: Futures Ease as Global Stocks Fall【原文：FTSE 100 Live: Futures Ease as Global Stocks Fall】

item.title: Two Chinese Supertankers U-Turn in Hormuz as Risks Remain High
item.description: Two Chinese-linked supertankers have U-turned in the Strait of Hormuz as risks to shipping remain elevated, with prospects for a normalization of traffic dimming after President Donald Trump took a hard line on Iran.

item.title: Nigeria Kicks Off Election Race With President in Pole Position
item.description: Campaigning for Nigeria’s January election is officially underway, with voters in Africa’s largest democracy offered the same slate of candidates as three years ago — and many of the same challenges.

item.title: Carry Traders Pivot to Swiss Franc After Yen Volatility Spikes
item.description: Carry traders are increasingly turning to the Swiss franc in the near term for their source of funding as the threat of intervention and higher interest rates saps the appeal of borrowing in the yen.

item.title: Unitree IPO: Why Investors Are Betting Big on China’s Humanoid Robots
item.description: Robots built to move, work and act like humans. It’s a global industry Morgan Stanley estimates could be worth $5 trillion by 2050. It’s also one of the frontiers in the China-US race for technological supremacy.

item.title: India’s Exports to US Hold Firm After a Year of Trump’s Tariffs
item.description: India’s share of exports to the US remained largely unchanged despite a year of President Donald Trump’s punitive tariffs and New Delhi’s efforts to diversify its trade with a raft of new deals with other countries.

item.title: Chinese Cartoon So Bad You Have to See It Becomes Box Office Hit
item.description: A low-budget cartoon about a calf has become an unlikely box-office sensation in China, turning online ridicule into millions of dollars in ticket sales and sparking a debate over the merits of crude animation in the age of polished AI-generated entertainment.

item.title: Hong Kong Exchange Posts Record Earnings on IPO, Trading Boom
item.description: Hong Kong’s stock exchange beat market estimates with a 21% rise in second-quarter net income, fueled by robust trading volumes and a jump in initial public offerings.

item.title: Korean Won Advances Past Key Psychological Level of 1,400 Per Dollar
item.description: The South Korean won strengthened past the key psychological level of 1,400 per dollar for the first time in more than 10 months, extending a recovery fueled by a booming semiconductor industry.
